claims.text: The starting alloy is nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11.
The starting alloy has a homogeneous solute distribution.
The intervention is a pre-irradiation vacuum anneal at approximately 550°C for 20 minutes.
The proposed anneal will induce Cr and V segregation without significant grain coarsening.
The anneal will increase the concentrations of Cr and V at grain boundaries.
Grain-boundary segregation of Cr and V will deplete Cr and V from grain interiors.
Solute depletion in grain interiors will reduce nucleation sites for radiation-induced precipitation.
Controlled solute segregation will reduce the local supersaturation that drives precipitate nucleation and growth during irradiation.
Grain boundaries will act as sinks for irradiation-induced defects.
Defect absorption at grain boundaries will maintain low irradiation hardening.
Untreated nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits radiation-induced precipitation under energetic-particle irradiation.
Untreated nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 exhibits negligible irradiation hardening.
At 300°C and approximately 8 dpa, the annealed alloy will have about 40% less radiation-induced precipitation than the untreated alloy.
At 300°C and up to approximately 8 dpa, irradiation hardening in the annealed alloy will remain below a 5% increase.
The proposed irradiation boundary is 300°C and up to approximately 8 dpa.
Annealing temperatures or dwell times that cause significant grain growth fall outside the hypothesis's applicable boundary.

contradictions.description: The predicted <5% irradiation-hardening increase appears to use the pre-irradiation state as its reference, whereas the falsification rule defines the 5% threshold relative to the untreated control. These are different comparators and could yield different decisions.
